record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given an undirected graph G and another graph H as the parameter, does H have an immersion in G, that is, can the vertices of H be mapped to vertices of G so that each edge of H corresponds to an edge-disjoint path of G?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An immersion of an undirected graph $H$ into an undirected graph $G$ is an injective mapping $\varphi:V(H)\to V(G)$ together with, for each edge $uv\in E(H)$, a path $P_{uv}$ in $G$ from $\varphi(u)$ to $\varphi(v)$, such that the paths $\{P_{uv}: uv\in E(H)\}$ are pairwise edge-disjoint.

Decide the following parameterized problem: given an undirected graph $G$ and an undirected graph $H$ (the parameter), does $H$ have an immersion in $G$? Specifically, determine whether this problem is fixed-parameter tractable with parameter $|H|$, i.e., whether there is an algorithm running in time $f(|H|)\cdot |V(G)|^{O(1)}$ for some computable function $f$.
artifact.status_search_result: Grohe, Kawarabayashi, Marx, and Wollan (STOC 2011; arXiv:1011.1827) proved that for every fixed graph H, there is an O(|V(G)|^3) algorithm deciding whether G contains H as a topological subgraph; as a corollary they obtain a cubic-time algorithm for H-immersion testing, establishing that the Immersion Order Test is fixed-parameter tractable. This resolved the open question of Downey and Fellows.

status_evidence.title: Finding topological subgraphs is fixed-parameter tractable
status_evidence.snippet: Grohe, Kawarabayashi, Marx, Wollan: cubic-time algorithm for fixed H topological subgraph and immersion testing.
status_evidence.claim: Immersion testing parameterized by H is FPT (in fact solvable in cubic time for each fixed H).
